payload.summary: Both amendments are confirmed by code investigation. Amendment fr-4-0d933f53 identifies a real correctness bug where Engine::from_parts() calls refresh_habitat_registry() before step_hours validation, causing light_exposure values to be recomputed with potentially invalid parameters. When validation subsequently fails, the returned state is partially mutated, violating the contract that failed steps leave state untouched. Amendment fr-4-7dfb6287 identifies a real debuggability deficiency where check_strictly_increasing only reports the upper field name and value in its error, omitting the lower bound field name even though it is available at all three call sites.

votes.rationale: Confirmed real bug. Engine::from_parts() at engine.rs:115 calls state.refresh_habitat_registry() which recomputes all habitat light_exposure values using the current intensity_index. In the failing test, intensity_index=1.4 causes light_exposure to be ~2x higher than the clone taken before from_parts(). When step_hours then calls enforce_invariants and validation fails (due to shrimp_assimilation_efficiency=1.2), the state has already been partially mutated via the habitat registry recomputation. This violates the documented contract that failed steps leave state untouched. Both proposed fixes (snapshot-restore or deferred recomputation) are sound.

Confirmed valid deficiency. check_strictly_increasing at invariants.rs:399-412 takes (lower_value, upper_field, upper_value) but never the lower field name. All three call sites have the lower field name readily available (e.g., 'shrimp_params.optimal_temp_min_c') but don't pass it through. The resulting error 'invariant violation for shrimp_params.optimal_temp_max_c with value X' gives no indication of which lower bound caused the failure. Adding the lower field name to the function signature and error message is a straightforward improvement that materially aids debugging.
